items.title: Territorial Acknowledgement
notes: Councillor Freeman opened the meeting with the following Territorial Acknowledgement:

As we recognize the National Day for Truth and Reconciliation on Wednesday, September 30, I acknowledge the Indigenous Peoples who have cared for these lands since time immemorial. I honour the Survivors of residential schools, the children who never returned home, and their families and communities. I recognize that reconciliation requires more than words; it calls for listening, learning, reflection, and meaningful action. I remain on a learning journey and am committed to deepening my understanding, confronting the ongoing impacts of colonialism, and carrying what I learn into my actions and relationships.

My own connection to the land has been shaped by living in Woodstock, Kitchener, and now Waterloo. I recognize Woodstock as being on the traditional territories of the Haudenosaunee, Lenape, and Anishinaabeg and within lands covered by the Upper Canada Treaties. I also recognize Kitchener and Waterloo as being on the Haldimand Tract, within the traditional territory of the Chonnonton, Anishinaabeg, and Haudenosaunee Peoples. As I reflect on the places I have called home, I am grateful for the land and waters that have sustained me, and I acknowledge my responsibility to learn about their histories, honour the enduring presence and contributions of Indigenous Peoples, and deepen my relationship with the land through respectful action.

We encourage everyone to take time to deepen their understanding of the residential school system and its lasting impacts. Reconciliation is not a single day or action. It is an ongoing commitment to building respectful relationships, advancing understanding and taking meaningful action. There are a number of events and activities that will take place in our community, and we encourage everyone to find the time to participate in some way. City services will remain open, but staff will spend time reflecting and learning.
As a City, we reaffirm our commitment to Reconciliation work, and to supporting a community where future generations can thrive.

items.title: Moment of Reflection
notes: Councillor Freeman provided Council with a moment of reflection.

The City of Waterloo extends its condolences to the family, friends and many colleagues of Dr. Ron Schlegel, whose remarkable contributions as an entrepreneur, educator, philanthropist and community builder have left a lasting impact in our community.

As a professor at the University of Waterloo, Ron played an important role in the development of health studies and gerontology, helping to strengthen the connection between academic research and the well-being of our community. His dedication to improving the lives of older adults continued through his work with Schlegel Villages and the Schlegel-UW Research Institute for Aging.

His entrepreneurial spirit, commitment to learning and remarkable generosity extended across many sectors, from agriculture and urban development to health care, including mental health and addiction care through Homewood Health Centre. He will be remembered as a community builder who helped make Waterloo Region a stronger and more connected place.

Ron was a true barnraiser in Waterloo Region, and his legacy is one of innovation, compassion and a commitment to community, his contributions to urban development, mental health and healthy aging continue to have an impact in Waterloo.
On behalf of the City of Waterloo, we extend our heartfelt condolences to Ron’s sons, their families, and all those who had the privilege of knowing and working with him.

items.title: THEMUSEUM
notes: David Marskell, CEO, THEMUSEUM gave a presentation updating Council on the organization’s recent accomplishments, highlighting the attendance records and fiscal successes. David Marskell also mentioned the “da Vinci Dialogues,” which are the speaker events they are holding this year, in connection with the Leonardo da Vinci exhibit they are hosting at THEMUSEUM. They held the opening last week, on September 23, which had a large turnout and was opened by Alessandro Cattaneo, the Italian Ambassador to Canada. David Marskell offered his thanks to the City and the community for their ongoing support. David Marskell then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: Bicycle Friendly Community Award Presentation
notes: Christopher Hodgson gave a presentation with an overview of the Bicycle Friendly Communities Program, and celebrated the achievement for the City to reach Platinum.

Waterloo and Ottawa are the only municipalities in Ontario to achieve this milestone. He further explained the framework for the program and the work involved in the City’s application. He then responded to questions of Council.

Matthew Riediger gave a presentation outlining the renovations coming to the Moses Springer Community Centre, including HVAC and other energy upgrades and modernizing the spaces to meet accessibility needs. He highlighted the teams and organizations that they received feedback from, as well as the funding breakdown. He then responded to questions of Council.

items.title: New Business
notes: Councillor Freeman spoke about many events that happened in the City. She highlighted the 25th anniversary for the Butterfly Learning Centre this past weekend, where she was joined by Mayor McCabe and MPP Catherine Fife. University of Waterloo also held their 23rd annual Pow Wow on Saturday, September 26, which looked like a great community event. Hospice Waterloo Region held a 3km hike on Sunday, September 27 to raise money to support the facility. Lastly, she mentioned that the Fox Hunt neighbourhood held their party in the park on Sunday, September 20.
Councillor Wright gave a shout-out to Lumen, which was on September 19, and offered thanks to the staff who run the event. It was a huge lift from the City to put on and it was very well attended.
